items.title: Pete Levin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001
items.q: I’d been listening to Jimmy Smith, like everybody, and trying to emulate him

ctx.x: Larry Young. Sometimes I get a lot of coffee and I’m racing and racing, and then my thoughts get left — Larry Young is just amazing. There was a big turnaround for me, I think somewhere in the 70s, because I’d been listening to Jimmy Smith, like everybody, and trying to emulate him, which of course you can’t do but it’s fun to try, there’s just so much spirit in his playing. And I went to — I remember the concert but I don’t remember who was headlining it, but John McLaughlin was the opening act. No, Tony…
it was the original, Tony Williams Lifetime. But first — you’re making me think of that stuff.
